title: The ERCP Theory and the UCEC Turbine: Energy Conversion in Large Incompressible Moving Masses
content:
This paper proposes the Energy Restoration by Planetary Fields (ERPF) theory, a new paradigm for understanding energy conversion in oceanic flows. Unlike classical models that treat energy as a finite and locally extractable resource, the ERPF theory considers the ocean as an open, dynamic system, where the kinetic energy of large incompressible masses — characterized by high density and volumetric stability — is continuously restored by planetary forces. This inherent inertia allows local energy capture without significant impact on the global flow dynamics.
The paper also introduces the UCEC (Current Energy Collecting Unit), a turbine specifically designed to operate in resonance with the flow, ensuring efficient energy capture with minimal disruption to the system. The theoretical foundations are presented alongside the innovative geometry of the UCEC, and an experimental validation plan is outlined. The work opens new possibilities for renewable energy conversion, suggesting a pathway toward sustainable, large-scale harvesting of oceanic kinetic energy.
